- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.5) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- If model shows sharp upward spike followed by forecast overshoot, apply downward correction of 2–5% in subsequent days.  
- If true outcome is significantly below forecast (especially after a spike), check if sentiment was high — if so, assume model overreacted; apply mean reversion bias correction.  
- If sentiment is negative or neutral (≤0.3) and forecast is high, reduce forecast by 2–4% to align with mean reversion or bearish sentiment.  
- For 30-day horizon, if forecast is consistently above true outcome by >5% over 3–5 days, apply a “lag correction” — reduce forecast by 1–2% per day for the next 3–5 days.  
- If sentiment history shows strong positive momentum followed by a drop, model often overcorrects — reduce forecast by 1–3% in the next 2–3 days.  
- If true outcome is below 65% of historical mean, model often overestimates — apply downward bias correction of 3–5% for next 3–5 days.
